scientific_name: Mandevilla x amabilis 'Sun Parasol Giant White'

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed when soil and air are warm; in zone 9 plant March-May. Sun Parasol Giant White is the pure-white member of the large-flowered Giant group within the Sun Parasol mandevilla line. The plant twines naturally and needs a trellis, fence, pergola, or other structure to climb.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in well-drained, fertile, slightly acidic to neutral soil, giving Sun Parasol Giant White a trellis, obelisk, or fence to climb from the start. Its oversized, pure-white, funnel-shaped flowers can span up to five inches across and open continuously against glossy deep green foliage from late spring through frost, making it one of the showiest white-flowered vines available for a Gulf South summer. The large trumpet blooms draw hummingbirds reliably and show up strongly against darker backdrops or evening light. In zone 9a this cultivar has no reliable cold hardiness: bring container specimens indoors or treat as an annual before the first fall frost, since even a light freeze will kill the foliage and stems.

planting.note: Transplant after frost danger passes into a container or bed with light support, as this compact Rio series selection suits patio culture and self-branches without heavy pinching.

directions: Site Rio White in full sun with rich, well-drained soil, allowing it to mound in a container or trail from a hanging basket rather than training it up a tall trellis like older vining mandevillas. Crisp white, funnel-shaped flowers open in repeated flushes against glossy foliage all summer with little deadheading needed. Water when the soil surface dries and feed every two to three weeks during active growth to sustain bloom. In zone 9a this cultivar has no cold tolerance, so move containers indoors or treat as an annual well before the first fall frost, since temperatures near freezing will damage or kill the plant.
sources: Syngenta Flowers — Rio White Dipladenia variety page

planting.note: Set out after all danger of frost has passed, giving the vine a trellis, arbor, or low wall to twine on from the start. Red Riding Hood is an older Mandevilla sanderi selection grown for its deep pink, yellow-throated flowers and remains widely sold alongside newer Sun Parasol and Rio introductions.

directions: Grow Red Riding Hood in full to partial sun in enriched, well-drained, slightly acidic soil, training the twining stems onto a trellis, arbor, or raised-bed railing since this older selection climbs more than the newer compact Rio and Garden-type mandevillas. Deep pink, funnel-shaped flowers with bright yellow throats appear in a steady profusion from spring through the first fall frost on glossy, dark-green evergreen foliage. Prune lightly each year to control size and encourage branching, and wear gloves when cutting since the milky sap can irritate skin. This cultivar is hardy only in USDA zones 10-11, so zone 9a gardeners should grow it in a container and move it to a sheltered, frost-free location well before the first freeze.
